description: Desarrollador apasionado por la exploración espacial y la inteligencia artificial, enfocado en crear un software autónomo de monitorización biométrica para astronautas en misiones de larga duración. Mi objetivo es construir una plataforma resistente y capaz de diagnosticar la salud fisiológica y cognitiva de la tripulación en tiempo real, operando de forma 100% local sin depender de la Tierra.
summary:
KHIPU SPACE is a crew health self-check app for long space missions. Each astronaut's health is shown as a digital khipu, the knotted-cord record of the Andes: one cord per indicator, one knot per day. Knot size shows how far today is from that person's own in-flight baseline, and a glowing cord marks a sustained change.

Behind it runs SENTINEL, an engine that learns each crew member's personal baseline with a Kalman filter and raises one explained alert when evidence builds up (CUSUM), calibrated to a fixed false-alarm budget. The app works offline, adapts its advice to how fast the flight surgeon can be reached, and matches its indicators to NASA's Spaceflight Standard Measures.

This matters because far from Earth the crew must notice slow, personal changes themselves, and population ranges miss them. On real wearable data from 64 people on Earth, SENTINEL detected 61% of injected 10-day events versus 35% for a fixed threshold at the same alert rate. Daily astronaut data are not public, so every profile is labelled as real or simulated.
details:
How it works Each crew member signs in on the tablet and does a short daily check-in. KHIPU SPACE draws their health as a khipu: one cord per indicator, one knot per day. The SENTINEL engine learns each person's own in-flight baseline (Kalman filter), accumulates evidence of sustained change (CUSUM) and opens one explained alert, showing which cords caused it and what to do next. Benefits Earlier detection of slow, personal changes that population ranges miss, with few false alarms. It works offline and adapts its advice to how quickly the flight surgeon can be reached, from the space station to a Mars conjunction with no contact. Intended impact Support crew autonomy on long missions, and offer the same personal-baseline approach for remote settings on Earth.

Tools Python (engine, simulator, experiments, tests), JavaScript, HTML and CSS (offline web app), GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages. Data: LifeSnaps wearable dataset (CC BY 4.0). AI assistance was used for coding and drafting, with human review by the team. Creativity The interface is built on Andean heritage, and every element has a job: the khipu is the record, tambos are body systems, the Qhapaq Ñan shows contact with the ground, tocapu motifs identify systems without relying on colour, and the amauta is the offline guide. What we considered Honesty about data (real and simulated profiles are labelled; no astronaut data are invented), alignment with NASA's Spaceflight Standard Measures, alarm fatigue, accessibility, and privacy: data stay on the device. It is a prototype, not a medical device.
